title: 🚕 GTA VI Reveals Ride-Share Fast Travel System
description: Rockstar's latest GTA VI details reveal that players can use ride-share vehicles as a fast-travel option while exploring Leonida.
article_content:
Grand Theft Auto VI will give players a new way to move around its massive world without driving everywhere themselves.

New details from Game Informer's GTA VI coverage reveal that ride-share vehicles can be used as a fast-travel option across Leonida. Players can ride as passengers while the driver takes them toward their destination.

The feature also includes additional interactions during the journey. Passengers can listen to conversations and browse the in-game Snapmatic social app while travelling.

The system gives players another option for crossing Leonida when they want to focus on exploration rather than spending time behind the wheel.

description: Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball says GTA VI pre-orders are breaking records on Xbox, while the platform's share reportedly matches its overall console market position.
article_content:
Grand Theft Auto VI pre-orders are reportedly setting new records on Xbox ahead of the game's November launch.

Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball pushed back against reports suggesting that GTA VI pre-orders are heavily concentrated on PlayStation 5. Ball said Xbox is very happy with the game's pre-order performance and that GTA VI is breaking records on the platform.

He also said Microsoft's internal analysis shows Xbox's share of GTA VI pre-orders is broadly matching its share of the overall console market. However, Microsoft has not published exact pre-order figures, so the precise platform split remains unknown.

description: The first six GTA VI: The Album songs have reportedly surpassed 24 million Spotify streams, with the full 34-track album still unreleased.
article_content:
Grand Theft Auto VI's upcoming soundtrack is already attracting millions of streams before the full album launches.

The six released tracks from GTA VI: The Album have reportedly passed 24.2 million combined Spotify streams. The songs initially generated around 4.1 million combined streams during their first 24 hours, according to industry reporting.

Morgan Wallen's 'Last Thing You Need' is currently the biggest performer among the released songs, with more than 6.8 million Spotify streams.

title: 🎨 Rockstar Explains Why GTA VI Isn't Going Fully Photorealistic
description: Rockstar North says GTA VI is designed to feel realistic rather than chase pure photorealism, helping the game's visual style remain strong over time.
article_content:
Rockstar North has explained the visual philosophy behind Grand Theft Auto VI, saying the game is designed to feel realistic rather than simply look photorealistic.

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained that the studio believes pure photorealism can age poorly as technology advances. Instead, GTA VI uses a carefully controlled visual style that combines realistic environments, characters and lighting with Rockstar's traditional artistic direction.

The approach is intended to help the game's world remain visually convincing for years while keeping characters and action readable during gameplay.

The philosophy continues Rockstar's long-running preference for stylized realism rather than completely photorealistic visuals.

article_content:
Rockstar Games has officially revealed a new premium merchandise collection for Grand Theft Auto VI.

The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection is priced at $399.99 and includes 11 Vice City and Leonida-themed items, including a Macca the Gator figure, Oakley sunglasses, a Leonida Keys crossbody bag, a New Era hat, collectibles, stickers and a double-sided Leonida map poster.

Rockstar Games has brought the world of Grand Theft Auto VI into real-life Miami with a massive new promotional installation.

A giant 'Welcome to Vice City' sign has been installed on the roof of the Kaseya Center, directly connecting GTA VI's fictional setting with the real city that inspired Vice City.

title: 🎵 GTA VI Album's Hidden Track Order Revealed
description: The official GTA VI: The Album pre-save listing has revealed the numbered positions of all 34 tracks, although most artists and song titles remain hidden.
article_content:
Fans have discovered that Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album's official pre-save listing already contains the numbered positions for all 34 tracks.

Rockstar and Atlantic Records have announced six singles so far, but the remaining 28 songs have not yet been publicly identified. The album listing nevertheless reveals where the released songs appear in the final 34-track sequence.

Yung Lean's 'That's It' occupies track 2, Travis Scott's 'RHYNO' is track 4, 'Sexy Magic' appears at track 5 and Morgan Wallen's 'Last Thing You Need' is track 8. Rauw Alejandro's 'Macacoa 2000' is listed at track 11, while Keith Richards' 'Bright Lights, Big City' appears at track 32.

The remaining positions are currently shown without publicly revealed artists or titles, leaving fans with 28 unidentified tracks to discover before the album launches.

description: Grand Theft Auto VI has received an MA 15+ classification in Australia, while final ESRB and PEGI ratings have yet to be published.
article_content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has received an official classification in Australia ahead of its November launch.

The Australian Classification Board has classified GTA VI as MA 15+, providing one of the first official age classifications for Rockstar's upcoming open-world game.

The classification comes while GTA VI's final ESRB and PEGI ratings remain pending. Rockstar's own website continues to display the game's ESRB rating as pending, meaning players should not treat unofficial predictions about the final US or European ratings as confirmed.

The Australian classification gives players another indication of how the game is being assessed by international rating authorities before release.

Grand Theft Auto VI is currently scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: 🗺️ GTA VI's Early Leonida Map Reportedly Reaches FiveM
description: A decade-old prototype of the GTA VI map has reportedly been made to run through FiveM, giving developers a technical look at an early version of Leonida.
article_content:
An extremely early version of the Grand Theft Auto VI map has reportedly been ported into FiveM.

The map is believed to come from Rockstar development material dating back to 2014 or 2015 and represents an unfinished version of Leonida from an early stage of GTA VI's development.

The project was reportedly created by a FiveM user known as Glowabl3, who demonstrated that the old map could technically run within the multiplayer framework. However, the creator has reportedly decided not to release a public server because of Rockstar and Cfx.re rules surrounding leaked and external game assets.

The discovery does not represent the final GTA VI map and should not be treated as an indication of what the launch version will contain. Instead, it provides another glimpse at how dramatically the game's world has evolved during development.

description: Platform and support documentation reportedly indicates that GTA VI may become playable at midnight on November 19 in each region rather than at one global launch time.
article_content:
Grand Theft Auto VI could use a region-by-region midnight release schedule when it launches on November 19.

Reports based on platform store and support documentation indicate that the game may unlock at midnight local time in each region rather than becoming available simultaneously worldwide.

This could mean players in New Zealand and other parts of the Asia-Pacific region receive access before players in Europe and North America, depending on their local time zones.

Rockstar Games has confirmed the November 19 release date and the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S launch platforms, but it has not published a detailed worldwide unlock schedule or officially explained the timing.

description: Rockstar has published updated modding guidelines ahead of GTA VI, placing new restrictions on fan-made story content, ports and unauthorized multiplayer projects.
article_content:
Rockstar Games has introduced updated modding guidelines just weeks before Grand Theft Auto VI launches.

The new rules place stricter limits on certain types of fan-made content, including new story expansions, cross-game ports and unauthorized multiplayer experiences. The guidelines are intended to clarify what types of modifications are permitted across Rockstar's games.

The changes arrive as the GTA community prepares for GTA VI and follows years of growth around major multiplayer modification projects connected to the Grand Theft Auto series.

Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA VI, but the updated policy provides an early indication of how the company intends to approach modifications surrounding its games going forward.

title: 🧍 GTA VI Will Have Rockstar's Most Diverse NPCs Yet
description: Rockstar says GTA VI features its most physically varied NPC population yet, with a new animation system allowing characters of different heights and body shapes to move naturally.
article_content:
Grand Theft Auto VI is taking another major step toward creating a more believable open world with a significantly more varied NPC population.

Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson explained that the game uses a new animation-retargeting system that allows animations to adapt dynamically to characters with different heights and body proportions.

This means pedestrians across Vice City and Leonida can have greater physical variation while still performing animations naturally. Rockstar says the system allows GTA VI to create a more diverse population than any previous game from the studio.

The technology is another example of Rockstar focusing on small details that can make Leonida feel more alive and realistic when the game launches.
